ov: Africa's social big cat. Lions live in prides of related females and their cubs, defended by one or a few males, and a small population also survives in India's Gir Forest.

why.ac: Mostly active at night and around dawn and dusk; lions spend much of the hot day resting.

rg: Savanna, grassland and open woodland in sub-Saharan Africa, plus Gir National Park in western India. Historically absent from the central African rainforest and the Sahara.
df: Mostly medium and large hoofed animals such as wildebeest, zebra, buffalo and gemsbok.

cf.tip: Both are plain tawny cats, but a cougar is much smaller, lives in the Americas, and has a long, thick tail with no dark tuft at the end.

fx: A lion’s roar, most often heard at night, carries up to about 8 km.
notes: Length/weight are ADW's species-wide ranges (both sexes, tail included). why.ac "much of the day resting" is standard; the Wikipedia Behaviour section covers it. rg adds India to the page's "Found in: Africa".
